text:
liam (Support): Heads-up — Customer 'BrightCart' reporting identical rerank payloads returning different score orders since yesterday's canary. They sent a repro set of 20 queries, same JSON each time, 5 of them now show swapped top-2 compared to baseline. Request id: req_94a3b2. Sys shows 200 but ranks differ. https://redwood.internal/logs/req_94a3b2 :thinking_face:
maya (CS): Ack. Do we know which model variant was on canary? Any quantization involved?
liam (Support): Canary used model v2-qa-quant (int8 hybrid) on 1% traffic per rollout notes. Customer said behavior started ~2024-06-01 16:00 UTC. They included curl repro:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"query":"where is my order","candidates":["Order #12345","Shipping info","Order status","Contact support"],"max_candidates":4}'
```
maya (CS): Good repro. Did they mutate whitespace or encoding? sometimes normalization differences bite.
jordan (ML Eng): Uploaded the model bench artifacts — I see v2-qa-quant uses different kernel path and a new batching heuristic. Quick check: quantized inference should be deterministic given same inputs, unless there's nondeterministic GPU kernels or batching mixing shard boundaries.
sam (SRE): Correlating logs: canary saw requests routed to pool-gpu-08 with driver 545.85, and pool-gpu-04 (older) with driver 535.x for baseline. Different drivers could cause fp32 fallback ops.
liam (Support): Customer insists payload identical bytes. They also attached curl with --data-binary to show exact bytes.
maya (CS): I pulled their attachment — there are trailing spaces and a \n between some candidates in a couple queries. Could be tokenization differences between kernel versions.
jordan (ML Eng): Repro locally: ran exact payload against v2-qa-quant and v2-qa-fp32, got rank flip on candidate 2/20. When I enable single-threaded execution and disable async batching, results match baseline. With our default continuous batching, nondeterminism shows. Hypothesis: batch reorder + int8 kernel nondeterministic accumulation.
sam (SRE): For triage: can we pin BrightCart's traffic to v2-qa-fp32 until we sort? Also capture full trace ids for affected requests.
liam (Support): Already suggested pin; customer agreed to temporary pin. I'll apply via admin console and confirm.
jordan (ML Eng): Steps I ran to reproduce: 1) run the exact curl payload (attached) 2) call /internal/debug?trace=req_94a3b2 to get KV cache dumps 3) compare tokenized sequences between variants (we saw small whitespace tokens added). Repro script:
```python
# quick check
import requests
PAYLOAD = {...}
for model in ['v2-qa-fp32','v2-qa-quant']:
  r = requests.post('https://staging.redwood/v1/rerank', json=PAYLOAD, headers={'x-model':model})
  print(model, r.json()['ranks'])
```
Result: ranks differ only when batching=true on quant variant.
maya (CS): Customer asked if this is a bug or expected quantization degradation. How to explain?
jordan (ML Eng): Short: quantization + asynchronous batching + slight tokenizer differences can amplify small logits differences into rank flips for near-ties. It's a stability/regression issue, not "random" per se. We'll need: deterministic kernel path for quant variant or better tie-breaking rules in rerank.
sam (SRE): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pin BrightCart to fp32 2) Rollback canary to 0% on quant model 3) Create a canary smoke test that runs a curated rerank set comparing key customer queries and fails the rollout if reorder occurs
maya (CS): I'll send customer a clear status update: pinned, investigating, ETA ~24h.
liam (Support): Customer also reported one 429 earlier during repro; I traced it to their client replays hitting rate limit while we were re-running tests. Not related to ranking but noted.
jordan (ML Eng): Long-term options: deterministic quant kernels (we have branches), update token normalization to be canonical before model input, or add stable-sort on logits with deterministic tie-breaker (e.g., candidate id hashed). I'll prototype the tie-breaker today.
sam (SRE): Also add a trace-level flag to force single-request inference for critical customers so batching doesn't change their results.
maya (CS): Assigned follow-ups: @jordan prototype tie-breaker + deterministic path, @sam add smoke test + canary rollback rule, @liam coordinate customer comms and pinning.
ops-bot: Created ticket RFC-1129: "rerank: quantization canary introduces nondeterministic ranking for near-ties" assigned to eng-ml, severity P2.
liam (Support): Customer updated: appreciates pin but wants ETA on root cause. I'll keep them posted and share repro script.
maya (CS): Thanks team. Keep thread updated. If anyone finds a quick config flag to force deterministic kernels, drop it here. :pray:
